finding_key: packages/backend/src/image/image.controller.ts::`delete /images/:id` is authenticated but performs no ownership/workspace authorization — any signed-in user who knows an image url can delete another workspace's image (idor)
evidence: The supplied image.controller.ts DELETE handler (the `@Delete(':id')` block, ~lines 55-63) guards only with `JwtAuthGuard`, validates the id against `VALID_IMAGE_ID_PATTERN`, then calls `imageService.delete(id)`, which issues a bare `DeleteObjectCommand` on the shared bucket (image.service.ts `delete`) with no owner/workspace check — so authorization is authentication-only, exactly as claimed. The legacy flat namespace is real too: `docsImageUploader` in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts POSTs to `${BACKEND_BASE}/images` with no `keyPrefix`, so frontend-uploaded doc/slide images live at bare `<uuid>.<ext>` keys, and those ids are visible in every rendered `src`, meaning any signed-in user (including a read-only collaborator) can delete them. Scope caveat: the id pattern means workspace-prefixed keys written by the v1 controller (`{workspaceId}/{id}`) can't be reached through this route, and the defect is pre-existing rather than introduced by this diff — the diff only touches rest-api.md prose and slides export — so it is an accurate observation about existing code rather than a regression in the change under review; I could not independently confirm `VALID_IMAGE_ID_PATTERN` since image.constants.ts was not supplied, but the flat-key delete path is visible in the excerpts.
